findings.title: excludes all causes and admits one
findings.claim: The negative prevention clause leaves the people's saying as the sole stated cause of their not believing.
findings.mechanism: Mā opens the negative frame, illā restricts it, and nominalized saying fills the remaining cause slot.
findings.reader_payoff: The cause is identified as an act the people themselves perform.
findings.containment: This is restriction within the clause, not an exhaustive account of outside causes.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: believing and saying routed through the pivot
findings.claim: The first an-clause makes believing the blocked act; the later an-clause makes saying the exception's cause.
findings.mechanism: The first governs subjunctive belief, while the second packages completed speech after illā.
findings.reader_payoff: An unrealized act is placed opposite a completed utterance.
findings.containment: The particles share form but perform distinct jobs.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: exception closes negation into restriction
findings.claim: Illā closes the negative-exception frame by restricting the preventer to the following saying clause.
findings.mechanism: It follows negated prevention and introduces the cause that remains.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence turns from withholding the cause to naming it.
findings.containment: This is a local construction, not a ranking of causes.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: particle preserves completed aspect
findings.claim: The nominalizing an preserves qālū as a completed utterance while making it the exception's cause.
findings.mechanism: Nominalization changes the clause's role without turning the perfect event hypothetical or future.
findings.reader_payoff: The obstruction is something already said.
findings.containment: Aspect belongs to qālū; the particle introduces its clause.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: nominalized saying resolves the preventer
findings.claim: The nominalized saying supplies the delayed cause required by the earlier prevention predicate.
findings.mechanism: Mana'a leaves the preventer unnamed until illā an qālū identifies the speakers' act.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening obstruction connects to the act disclosed at the end.
findings.containment: This names the stated cause without settling motives beyond the question.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: matching particles set believing against saying
findings.claim: The two an clauses place believing and saying in opposite roles: one is blocked, the other names the blocker.
findings.mechanism: The first governs imperfect subjunctive belief; the second introduces completed speech under the exception.
findings.reader_payoff: Matching particles bind the pair while syntax reverses their roles.
findings.containment: The particles are not interchangeable in their clauses.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: speech-act made the exception item
findings.claim: The second an turns completed saying into the single cause retained by the exception.
findings.mechanism: An packages the perfect speech clause into the exception's cause position.
findings.reader_payoff: A whole speech-act is compressed into the item left after illā.
findings.containment: This is grammar, not judgment about the utterance's truth.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: completed saying functions as barrier
findings.claim: The people's completed qālū clause is presented as the act obstructing their believing.
findings.mechanism: The perfect plural heads the nominalized exception clause and fills mana'a's cause slot.
findings.reader_payoff: Their speech is part of the obstruction, not only evidence of it.
findings.containment: Qālū means saying; causal force comes from the construction.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: direct speech embeds an incredulous question
findings.claim: Qālū introduces the following interrogative clause as the content of what the people said.
findings.mechanism: The question attaches as quoted content inside the stated cause.
findings.reader_payoff: The barrier includes both speaking and the challenge spoken.
findings.containment: It is quoted speech, not a narrator's assertion.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.title: recorded utterance rather than command to speak
findings.claim: The perfect form records a completed utterance rather than commanding anyone to speak.
findings.mechanism: QAC marks qālū as perfect inside a report of what they said.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse diagnoses an utterance already made.
findings.containment: This is a contrast in form and clause function.

epistemic.reason: Focus surface and trusted aligned support directly establish this bounded local relation.

findings.reader_payoff: The affected group is heard again as the group speaking.
